clinician.final_diagnosis: K. pneumoniae endogenous endophthalmitis (EE) with wide retinal necrosis in a previously healthy subject
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 72-year-old immunocompetent male presented with acute prostatitis due to ampicillin-resistant K. pneumoniae (>100,000 CFU/ml urine) and was started on IV gentamycin. Three days after admission, he developed floaters and vision loss in the right eye (E002), consistent with metastatic endogenous endophthalmitis. Ophthalmologic examination revealed hand motion vision, severe anterior chamber inflammation with fibrin, and opaque fundus view (E004). B-scan ultrasonography demonstrated vitreous chamber hyper-reflective signal compatible with abscess or hemorrhage (E004). He underwent urgent pars plana vitrectomy with intravitreal vancomycin and ceftazidime (E005). Intraoperative findings included moderately ischemic retina with vasculitis and retinal infiltration temporal to the fovea (E006). The clinical course was complicated by progressive retinal pathology necessitating a second pars plana vitrectomy with silicone oil tamponade (implied by subsequent silicone oil removal). At 10-month follow-up, silicone oil was removed with retina attached, laser photocoagulation performed around retinal defects, and visual function improved (E014). Final best corrected visual acuity stabilized at 0.3 (E015).
